notes_list.basic_overview: Aldehydes can be selectively oxidized to carboxylic acids using sodium chlorite under controlled conditions.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Pinnick oxidation is particularly useful when mild and selective aldehyde-to-acid conversion is needed. Scavengers such as sulfamic acid or related additives may be used to manage chlorite-derived side products.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
Sodium chlorite oxidizes the aldehyde through chlorite-derived oxidizing intermediates while scavengers suppress side reactions, giving the carboxylic acid.
